summary: Wilhelm Schulze was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Schmidt, at Greifswald under Zimmer, Kießling, and Kaibel, and under Wilamowitz-Moellendorff. He held posts at Marburg (1892), Göttingen (1895), and Berlin (1902–1932).
Wilhelm Schüler was a sinologist who held a professorship at the Seminar for Oriental Languages (Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin) from circa 1904 to 1935.
Wilhelm Solf was an Indologist. He studied at Berlin, Jena, Göttingen, Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, and Kiel University, where he later held a post from circa 1888 to 1889.
Wilhelm Storck studied under Franz Bopp and Moriz Haupt.

Wilhelm Streitberg was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Münster, Berlin, and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and Ernst Windisch. He held posts at Fribourg (~1889–1898), Münster (1899), Munich (1909), and Leipzig (1898, 1920–1925).

Wilhelm Wackernagel worked in linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1824–1827) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He later taught at Pädagogium Basel (~1833–1835) and held a professorship at the University of Basel (1833; 1835–1869).

Wilhelm Wundt worked in philosophy. He studied at the universities of Tübingen, Heidelberg, and Berlin between 1851 and 1856. He later held posts at the University of Zurich (1857), Leipzig University (1858), and Heidelberg University (1864).

Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Viadrina, Göttingen, and Jena under teachers including Campe, Engel, von Dohm, Klein, Lichtenberg, Heyne, and de Chézy, and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1809–1810).
Will B. Miller specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso and also studied under Lopen Chorten in 2012.
Will Sweetman is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and the University of Cambridge. He held a post at the University of Otago around 2004.

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby was a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard. He taught at McGill (1960–1964) and Yale (1966–1971), and held posts at Trinity College and the University of Toronto (1971–1999).
Willard J. Peterson is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. Mentored by Denis Twitchett, he held a professorship at Princeton University, attested in 1981.

Willard Van Orman Quine worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at Oberlin College and Harvard University. His career included posts at Harvard (1940–1978), Wesleyan University (1964–1965), and the University of Oxford (~1973–1974).

Willem Bollée was an Indologist. He studied at Utrecht University and the University of Hamburg. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and as a lecturer and professor at Heidelberg University (~1970–1992).

Willem Caland was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Carel Gabriel Cobet. He held posts at Utrecht University (1902; 1906–1929) and Leiden University (1913–1914).

Willem van der Molen is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1971–1983) and held posts at Leiden University (~1979–2017) and the University of Indonesia.
William Blackstone studied at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College (~1738–1745). He held a post at the University of Oxford from circa 1753 to 1766.

William C. Chittick works in religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tehran (~1966–1974) and held posts at Sharif University of Technology (~1974–1979), SUNY Albany (~1980–1983), and Stony Brook University (~1983).

William C. Kirby works in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Dartmouth and at Harvard under Philip A. Kuhn. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1980–1992) and Harvard University (~1992).
William Carey worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Ramram Basu and Golok Nath Sharma, and was appointed Professor of Sanscrit, &c. at Fort William College in 1801.
